newsitem.title: UK: Mideast VLCCs softer but some see tightness ahead.
newsitem.headline: Mideast VLCCs softer but some see tightness ahead.

text.p: Middle East very large crude carriers (VLCCs) held a softer tone on Friday, failing to maintain the momentum achieved earlier in the week, but some brokers saw firm rates over the next four weeks on a tightness of tonnage.

Brokers Galbraith's Ltd said that although modern ships to South Korea achieved up to W74.5 early in the week, "the general tone of the market is one of falling rates, so one should expect the next deal to be a few points lower."

But E.A. Gibson said in their weekly tanker report that despite the recent dip, "we predict only 43 vessels of about 12.5 million tons being available during the next four weeks and, therefore, the market should remain firm."
Galbraith's said older tonnage was particularly vulnerable to further falls with such ships achieving only about W62/65.

But they added that "Monday should see stem confirmations from many Middle East suppliers for July which should result in fresh business, particularly for modern units for the first half of that month.
"It is very difficult to predict what effect this willl have on the market, but at least for the next seven days, owners will surely find it extremely difficult to hold on to 'last done.'"
Galbraith's also said that very unusually, there was no Mideast/west or ultra-large (ULCC) business done this week.
According to a Galbraith's pie-chart, half of all VLCC/ULCC fixtures this year have been on Mideast/east routes -- 361, against 146 Mideast/west, 190 on non-Mideast routes and 49 Mideast/Red Sea.
Brokers said West Africa/U.S. Gulf and transatlantic VLCCs were little changed at around W67.5, while Suezmaxes (130,000 tonne vessels) in the former sector had dipped to below W90.

The Aframax (80,000 tonne) market remained firm, with cross-Med rates at W120, up some 10 points from last week, and that up to W155 had been offered. But cross-Med Suezmaxes dipped to around W85 on low enquiry, brokers said.
Inter-U.K./Cont Aframaxes were also strong at W130 on increased demand, with Suezmaxes healthy at W110.

The Caribs/upcoast market remains well below its year highs of around W240 for 70,000 tonne crude cargoes. But at W175/180 they are still firm compared to last year, when they averaged W148, according to New York-based Rigos Chartering Inc. --London newsdesk +44 171 542 4088
